extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) Benchmark
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark comprising 20,000 self-contradictory instructions designed to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in recognizing conflicting commands. It includes 10,000 language-language (L-L) and 10,000 vision-language (V-L) conflicts, distributed across eight tasks: RuleConflict, AttributeConflict, ExclusionConflict, ForbbidenConflict, OCRConflict, FigureConflict, GeometricConflict, and SemanticConflict.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, and Dequan Wang
extraction.citeAs: Gao, J., Gan, L., Li, Y., Ye, Y., & Wang, D. (2024). Dissecting Dissonance: Benchmarking Large Multimodal Models Against Self-Contradictory Instructions. arXiv:2408.01091.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed using a novel automatic dataset creation framework called AutoCreate, which leverages programs and Large Language Models (LLMs). The process involves generating initial data from seeds, creating contradictions via a 'Decorator', and filtering quality via a 'Cleaner'. Human experts manually checked the quality of the generated dataset and provided three levels of splits (SCI-Core, SCI-Base, SCI-All) based on conflict type frequency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of synthetic text and images generated by LLMs and programs. For SemanticConflict, images were retrieved from the ImageNet dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The AutoCreate framework manipulates data by generating initial seeds, creating self-contradictions (e.g., modifying image captions, altering chart data, generating opposite attribute descriptions), and cleaning data that does not meet quality standards. For V-L conflicts, image captions were modified to introduce conflicts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data was filtered by a 'Cleaner' component to remove entries not meeting quality standards. Human experts performed a double-check on the quality of the generated dataset. Subsets were manually selected to create SCI-Core (1%) and SCI-Base (10%) from the full SCI-All dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset items are inherently self-contradictory by design. The 'labels' or ground truth are the identification of the conflict. Evaluation of model responses was conducted by human experts and LLM agents (GPT-4, ChatGPT, ChatGLM) to determine if the model successfully identified the conflict.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Evaluation consistency between human experts and LLM agents was measured using Spearman correlation coefficient and concordance rate. GPT-4 showed close alignment with human evaluative standards.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work provides a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction. It promotes inclusivity in AI research through the AutoCreate framework and fosters trust and reliability in AI systems by improving dissonance detection.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms. It does not include fine-grained control to determine conflict degree. It does not provide a detailed study on the attention mechanism of LMMs when confronted with conflict instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is used to evaluate the capability of LMMs to decipher self-contradictory instructions and to test prompting techniques like Cognitive Awakening Prompting (CaP).
